verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Udaipur stone processors with quarry linkage and verified GST turnover; avoid single-customer, export-concentrated units until local demand data improves.
title: Udaipur stone, granite & marble processing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A stone processor buys quarry blocks, cuts and polishes them into slabs and tiles, and sells into construction, real estate and export markets.** Cash comes in per square metre or per cubic metre sold; the block is the single largest input cost, so a unit with group-owned quarries earns a structural margin the pure buyer never sees — ICRA notes one Rajasthan granite group meets around 40% of raw material from group-owned quarries [11]. **Ask every proposal what share of blocks is captive versus bought, and at what per-cbm rate; if captive share is nil, price the credit as a trading exposure, not a manufacturing one.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in block quality and finishing yield, not in volume.** Midwest's blended granite ASP was INR60,792/cbm [4], and its 1QFY27 revenue of INR1.9b rose 35% YoY but fell 11% QoQ on realisation [5] — so price, not tonnage, moves the P&L. **So when a proposal lands, check the receivable ageing by buyer and the inventory days of unsold slabs; if receivables exceed 90 days with one builder, ask for the buyer-wise ledger and a diversion clause.**

## What has changed now
**The local demand signal is weak even as national stone output is strong.** Rajasthan GST collections fell 4.7% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D], and state electricity demand grew 4.0% versus India's 9.5% [D] — both local stress markers. Nationally, IIP for NIC 23 stone output is +11.4% YoY and +10.2% Apr-to-date [D], so the growth is happening outside Rajasthan. **Peer results are mixed: Midwest recovered strongly QoQ [4] while Aro's June 2026 quarter net sales fell 23.72% YoY to Rs 20.62 crore [6].** Local sources are thin on Udaipur specifically — a MEAI seminar on smart mining [1] and a December GSTF 2026 stone-industry session [2] tell us the industry is organising, not that order books are filling. Treat the city read as first-principles plus peers.

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue processors with captive or group-leased quarry blocks, domestic builder supply contracts, and GST turnover that reconciles to bank credits.** Prefer units adding automated polishing or precision cutting, which Aro is investing in for premium granite [6]. **Take monthly GST returns, bank statements and a stock statement every month; if GST turnover falls below the drawing-base turnover for two consecutive months, freeze the limit and inspect stock.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch block inventory ageing and power consumption together.** A unit running polishing lines at falling electricity draw is cutting shifts — pull the CEA state demand trend [D] and ask for the plant's own meter readings. **Watch receivable days and buyer mix; a shift from builders to cash-and-carry dealers at a discount signals distress.** Watch the promoter's quarry lease renewals — a lapsed lease turns a captive-margin unit into a block buyer overnight. **If any of these three move adversely in one quarter, downgrade the internal grade and re-price before renewal.**
